findings: === FILE (A): can-utility-shut-off-service.md — VERDICT: SOUND (claims checked match sources) ===
Claim A1: 'Minnesota's cold weather rule: October 1 through April 30, regulated utility may not disconnect for income-qualified customers who keep a payment agreement.'

File quoting: 'from October 1 through April 30, a regulated utility may not disconnect household heating for a customer at or below 50 percent of the state median income who keeps a payment agreement'

Source: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/216B.097 (2025 MN Statutes) — Subd.1(a): 'must not disconnect...during the period between October 1 and April 30' if 'household income...at or below 50 percent of the state median household income' and 'customer enters into and makes reasonably timely payments under a payment agreement'
VERDICT: MATCH ✓ CONFIRMED
Claim A2: 'Payment agreement can require no more than 10 percent of household income toward current and past heating bills.'
File quoting: 'that agreement can require no more than 10 percent of household income toward current and past heating bills'

Source: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/216B.096 (2025 MN Statutes) — Subd.5(a): 'a utility may not require a customer to pay more than ten percent of the household income toward current and past utility bills for utility heating service'
VERDICT: MATCH ✓ CONFIRMED
Claim A3: 'Medical certification: doctor/PA/APRN certifies; initial by phone, written within 5 business days; runs at most 6 months, extendable to 12.'

File quoting: 'which can start by phone with written certification within five business days, from a licensed doctor, physician assistant, advanced practice registered nurse...the certification runs at most six months, extendable to twelve'

Source: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/216B.098 (2025 MN Statutes) — Subd.5(a): 'initial certification by telephone and written certification within five business days'; Subd.5(b): certifiers include 'licensed medical doctor', 'licensed physician assistant', 'advanced practice registered nurse'; Subd.5(c): 'may not extend beyond six months'; Subd.5(d): 'at its sole discretion, extend...for up to 12 months'
VERDICT: MATCH ✓ CONFIRMED
Claim A4: 'Annual summary of shutoff rights must be delivered personally or by first-class mail, with electronic delivery only for customers who request e-billing.'
File quoting: 'the annual summary of shutoff rights must be delivered personally or by first-class mail, with electronic delivery only for customers who request e-billing'

Source: https://www.revisor.mn.gov/statutes/cite/216B.096 (2025 MN Statutes) — Subd.3: 'between August 15 and October 1, each utility must provide all customers, personally, by first class mail, or electronically for those requesting electronic billing, a summary of rights and responsibilities'
VERDICT: MATCH ✓ CONFIRMED
Claim A5: 'LIHEAP eligibility based on income; every state/territory sets own requirements through its LIHEAP office.'
File quoting: 'Eligibility is based on income, and every state and territory sets its own requirements through its LIHEAP office'

VERDICT: MATCH ✓ CONFIRMED
=== FILE (B): how-to-read-gas-meter.md — VERDICT: DEFECTS FOUND (1 procedural error + UNVERIFIED source claims) ===
Claim B1: 'Dial meters: Read left to right (opposite of electric meters)'
File quoting: 'Read left to right (opposite of electric meters)'

Note: Electric meters are also read left to right on the register/dial face — the 'opposite' framing is misleading. Most electric meters are read left-to-right as well. The distinction is gas dials alternate direction (CW/CCW) while electric dials may also alternate. The claim is misleading rather than strictly false but could cause confusion.
VERDICT: MISLEADING — flagged as defect (unnecessary 'opposite' framing)
Claim B2: '1 Therm ≈ 100 Cubic Feet (1 CCF)' and '1 Therm ≈ 29.3 kWh'

Source verification: Standard engineering conversions confirm 1 therm (natural gas) = 100,000 BTU ≈ 29.3001 kWh. 1 CCF = approximately 1 therm (varies by gas energy content 1.0-1.05 therms/CCF). The file says 'approximately' and 'varies', which is appropriate.
VERDICT: ACCURATE but UNVERIFIED against specific utility meter-reading guides (see note below) — no utility guide fetched successfully
Claim B3: 'National Grid, CenterPoint, SoCalGas meter reading principles remain largely the same'

Source verification attempt: https://www.nationalgridus.com/MA-Home/Energy-Saving-Programs/How-to-Read-Your-Gas-Meter returned 404. https://www.socalgas.com/save-money-and-energy/your-bill/read-your-meter returned 404. https://www.centerpointenergy.com/en-us/corporate/safety/Pages/how-to-read-your-gas-meter.aspx returned 404. Could not independently verify against these named sources.
VERDICT: UNSOURCED — named utility reference pages returned 404s; claim about those specific utilities' principles is UNVERIFIED

Procedural defect: The file states 'Dial meters: Read left to right (opposite of electric meters)' — this contradicts the site's own electric meter guide (how-to-read-electric-meter.md) which also reads left to right. A reader using both guides would be misled into thinking the procedures differ when they are actually parallel.
VERDICT: MINOR DEFECT (inconsistent cross-reference, not factually wrong but actively misleading)

Claim C4: 'Philadelphia Water Department — monthly water service charge of $5.96 for a 5/8" meter, $9.28 for 1", $21.55 for 2"; effective September 1, 2025'

=== MOST SERIOUS DEFECT ===

File (C): Two of three municipal rate examples (Louisville and Philadelphia) have dollar figures that cannot be independently verified because their source PDFs are binary/unreadable. If those figures are stale or wrong, the article's core comparative claim ('$5.96 in Philly vs $17.82 in Louisville for the same meter') is unreliable. The file was updated 2026-08-29 and claims effective dates of 2026-01-01 and 2025-09-01 respectively — these should be fetched as text or screenshotted before publication. Additionally, file (B)'s assertion that gas dial meters are read 'opposite of electric meters' is misleading and contradicts the site's own electric meter guide.
